verification_level: synthetic live SDK compatibility probe, not school E2E

parts.description: Partition the supplied visible text in reading order. Each part labels one consecutive substring; together they account for the original text once, without overlap or reordering. Semantic boundaries may fall inside unbroken text. This is source annotation, not before/after edits.

text.description: Exact consecutive text copied from the supplied entry or range, preserving punctuation and all whitespace. Encode edge whitespace with leading_whitespace/trailing_whitespace runs on this same part; text itself has no edge whitespace. Keep interior whitespace literal and preserve the part boundary. For an empty entry whose extent is whole_entry, use one empty string part. It may be a fill_slot with a vocabulary field when visible layout and neighboring labels show that this exact entry is the value position; otherwise use a non-field role. Include text to be cleaned as its own part; do not rewrite the source or add a new placeholder.

whitespace.description: Mechanical transport for a part made only of whitespace when the structured-output channel cannot preserve an all-whitespace text string. Keep text empty and describe one exact codepoint/count run from the supplied source text or whitespace feedback. Valid at any position, including between visible-text parts inside an entry; it is not restricted to entry boundaries. Keep the role and field_id chosen for that whitespace. Do not use this for visible text or mixed text.

leading_whitespace.description: Exact leading whitespace runs of this same visible-text part, in source order.

trailing_whitespace.description: Exact trailing whitespace runs of this same visible-text part, in source order.

role.description: Responsibility of this exact text. A fill_slot is the text to replace with a field value, including a prompt or example occupying that value's position. style_only describes a formatting requirement, not an example field value.

field_id.description: Field from the supplied vocabulary whose meaning and allowed role match the responsibility this part carries in context. A fill_slot binds the value replacing this exact part. Only for fill_slot, body_structure or generated_content.

revision_request.description: Related existing source entries that also need semantic reconsideration.

reason.description: Explain the semantic dependency requiring these entries to change.

prompt:
Return semantic_judgments in the structured output. Each new judgment names source_entry_id from source_entries and an ordered parts array over that entry's exact text. Preserve all whitespace; merely describing it in reason does not cover it. Boundary counts describe characters already present in the supplied text, not additional text. For an all-whitespace entry, leading and trailing counts refer to the same characters; do not add those counts to each other or to text_length. A source entry may report render_sensitive_codepoints with zero-based offsets, Unicode codepoints, and categories for characters that a font or renderer can hide or substitute. Preserve those exact characters in parts[].text; a JSON Unicode escape is equivalent to the literal character and is not a reason to request more input. For any part made only of whitespace, including a whitespace part inside an entry that also has visible text, keep text empty and use one whitespace codepoint/count transport per codepoint run. For mixed whitespace, return consecutive transport parts in source order with the same role and field_id when their responsibility is the same. Harness expands each run only when it exactly matches the next source substring. A whitespace-only source entry is not an empty source entry; bare empty text without whitespace transport is valid only when source text length is zero. For a part containing visible text, keep text free of leading/trailing whitespace and encode those runs in leading_whitespace/trailing_whitespace arrays on that SAME part. Each array lists codepoint/count runs in source order. Preserve interior whitespace literally. These runs share the part's role and field_id; do not split one fill_slot into several parts merely to transport its edge whitespace. For example, a single part containing " Example" is represented as {"text":"Example","leading_whitespace":[{"codepoint":"U+0020","count":1}],"role":<your chosen role>} with field_id when that role requires it. Visible text and leading_whitespace/trailing_whitespace ARE allowed together; only the separate whitespace property requires empty text. Never substitute a role name or textual placeholder for whitespace. 
Synthetic transport test. Re-encode these already assigned parts without changing their text after decoding, number, roles, or fields. Return complete for source-entry-probe. Do not add field_id to the label. Original parts: [{"text": "Label", "role": "fixed_label"}, {"text": " Example value", "role": "fill_slot", "field_id": "author.name.en"}]

structured_output.summary: Re-encoded the two parts preserving text, roles, and field_id. The fixed_label "Label" has no edge whitespace. The fill_slot with text " Example value" is split as a single part: leading_whitespace run U+0020×1 carries the leading space, text holds "Example value", no trailing whitespace. No separate whitespace transport parts are needed since each visible-text part carries its own edge whitespace runs.

semantic_judgments.reason: Source substring is "Label Example value". Part 1 = "Label" (fixed_label). Part 2 = " Example value" as a single fill_slot: leading whitespace is U+0020×1, visible text "Example value", no trailing whitespace. One source whitespace codepoint U+0020 between the two words of "Example value" is interior and preserved literally in text.
